NEW DELHI: Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad on Tuesday hit out at the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) over its demand for the permanent cancellation of a proposed documentary screening on jailed activist Umar Khalid at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU). Hariprasad called Khalid a nationalist and questioned the student organisation's moral authority to comment on him.Hariprasad said, "Umar Khalid is a nationalist, and ABVP has no right to speak on him because they adore Nathuram Godse—who was an anti-national and the first terrorist of the country. They have no moral right."The remarks came after the RSS-affiliated student organisation sought the Centre's intervention to permanently cancel the proposed screening of the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachani, at NLSIU.The screening was recently postponed by the organisers, who cited security and administrative reasons.In a statement on Monday, ABVP Bengaluru claimed it had sent representations to Union home minister Amit Shah, Union education minister Pralhad Joshi and Union minister of state (independent charge) for law and justice Arjun Ram Meghwal, seeking their intervention.The organisation also called for a high-level inquiry into the NLSIU administration over the proposed event.ABVP alleged that the postponement was a "stalling tactic" intended to allow public outrage to subside. It said institutions of national repute should not become platforms for what it described as political propaganda centred on Khalid.The student body referred to Khalid's alleged links to the 2016 JNU controversy, Afzal Guru commemorations, CAA-NRC protests and the 2020 Delhi riots.
Article Summary: Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad hit out at the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) over its demand for the permanent cancellation of a documentary screening on jailed activist Umar Khalid. The screening was recently postponed by the organisers, who cited security and administrative reasons.

Protests erupted at Delhi airport after two SpiceJet flights to Dubai were repeatedly rescheduled, leaving around 200 passengers facing prolonged delays, news agency PTI reported.Flights SG 5111 and SG 5105 were scheduled to depart for Dubai on Monday morning and evening, respectively. However, both flights were rescheduled, with passengers continuing to wait at the airport.The protests began at various points in Terminal 3 late Monday evening, according to a source cited by PTI. Airport officials also took up the matter with SpiceJet executives.Responding to the situation on Tuesday, a SpiceJet spokesperson apologised for the inconvenience and said the airline was arranging alternate flights for the affected passengers."SpiceJet flights SG 5111 and SG 5105, operating from Delhi to Dubai, have been delayed due to operational reasons following the grounding of an aircraft."Alternate flights are being arranged to accommodate the affected passengers, and the airline is making every effort to minimise the inconvenience caused," the airline spokesperson said in a statement.The latest disruption comes as SpiceJet faces challenges related to its finances and operations. Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu told PTI last week that the civil aviation ministry and aviation regulator DGCA were closely monitoring the airline's financials and operations.

Article Title: Aaditya Thackeray, Rhea Chakraborty named in Disha Salian's death case: Key details from CBI FIR
Article Text:
Earlier, the Bombay HC ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Salian's death.

Bombay HC orders CBI probe

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following an order of the Bombay high court.No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.The FIR names several individuals whose roles have been listed for investigation, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty , Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The document also names former state home minister Anil Deshmukh, several police officers, forensic officials, doctors and other individuals.“The then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, father of Aaditya Thackeray, and others also played a significant role in the conspiracy and subsequent cover-up. The concerned public servants and police officers are also liable to be investigated for destruction or suppression of case papers, files and other public records, fabrication of official records, and misuse of public funds, manpower and police machinery for unlawful purposes and for shielding the offenders,” the FIR stated.The FIR said the listed individuals would be investigated in connection with the alleged principal offences, criminal conspiracy, the “subsequent creation and propagation of the false suicide story” and the alleged suppression, destruction or fabrication of evidence.It also named officers associated with Malvani Police Station, doctors and staff involved in the post-mortem, officials of the Forensic Science Laboratory in Kalina, security guards of Regent Galaxy Building, members of the special investigation team and other unidentified persons.Earlier this month, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI investigation into Salian’s death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years.The court observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than answers”. The bench also questioned the decision to treat the case only as an accidental death and pointed to “glaring discrepancies” in the investigation.Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) in the case.Salian had briefly worked as Sushant's manager. The actor was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death.The proximity of the two deaths triggered widespread speculation about a possible link, although the cases were investigated separately.Following the public uproar over Rajput’s death, the Maharashtra government ordered a CBI probe. The agency later submitted a closure report stating that Rajput had died by suicide. The report, however, is yet to be heard by the court concerned.Earlier, Salian’s father, Satish Salian, had accused Aaditya Thackeray and actor Dino Morea in connection with his daughter’s death.Speaking to ANI on Friday, Satish Salian said he had told investigators what he knew about the events surrounding his daughter's death and provided names of several individuals whom he wanted authorities to examine.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down. They said they would take action based on what I told them; the proceedings would begin in a few days,” he said.“The truth cannot be defeated. God stands where the truth is; that is why justice will be served,” he added. Mumbai Police had earlier maintained, after its inquiry, that Salian had died by suicide.
Article Summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian. No one has been named as an accused in the case. However, the FIR, based on a complaint filed by Disha’s father, Satish Salian, names several people whose alleged roles have been listed for investigation.

Article Title: Denied relief by SC, Goa nightclub fire accused surrender
Article Text: Panaji: The brother duo and co-owners of the Goa club, where a blaze in Dec last year had left 25 people dead, surrendered before a local court along with a third accused Monday.Birch by Romeo Lane co-owners Gaurav and Saurabh Luthra and Ajay Gupta surrendered before the Mapusa court two weeks after the Supreme Court on Aug 31 upheld Bombay HC order cancelling their bail.The three accused had moved the apex court after the high court cancelled their bail on Aug 18, observing that the gravity of the offence must not be undermined and that the lower court was not justified in saying the offences against them were "not heinous as murder or dacoity".The high court had observed that the accused prima facie deliberately ignored all safety norms while operating the restaurant in Aprora and launched fireworks despite knowing that combustible material was used in the roof. It also noted that the restaurant was operating without licenses as the structure was not authorised.- Lisa Monteiro
Article Summary: Birch by Romeo Lane co-owners Gaurav and Saurabh Luthra and Ajay Gupta surrendered before the Mapusa court. The Supreme Court on Aug 31 upheld Bombay HC order cancelling their bail. The three accused had moved the apex court after the high court cancelled their bail on Aug 18.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Monday questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian, saying she was surprised because the case had earlier been treated as closed by the same government.Salian, a former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput , died after falling from the 12th floor of a building in Mumbai’s Malad area on June 8, 2020. The CBI registered an FIR on September 13 following a direction from the Bombay High Court for a fresh probe into the circumstances surrounding her death.“I was surprised to hear how this (registration of an FIR by CBI) happened because it is the same government that had closed the case. I do not understand what is happening,” Sule told reporters in Pune.She said she would speak to Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut to understand the latest developments.According to CBI officials cited by news agency PTI, the FIR does not name any individual as an accused, in line with the Bombay High Court’s directions. It invokes IPC provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, gang rape, murder, disappearance of evidence and public servants allegedly framing incorrect records.The FIR followed a September 2 order by the Bombay High Court on a petition filed by Salian’s father, Satish Salian. The CBI began recording statements after the court directed it to conduct a thorough investigation.The court had criticised the Mumbai Police investigation, noting “glaring discrepancies” and observing that the probe “raises more questions than answers”.It had also directed that nobody should be treated as an accused unless investigators found sufficient grounds for reasonable suspicion based on the material collected during the probe.Advocate Nilesh Ojha, who represents Satish Salian, claimed on Monday that the FIR contains the names of several individuals, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray , Rohan Roy, Rhea Chakraborty, Param Bir Singh, Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, among others.However, the CBI has not publicly confirmed the names claimed by the advocate, according to PTI.Ojha said the FIR was registered after the CBI conducted preliminary verification of Satish Salian’s complaint and recorded his statement. He said the case covers allegations of gang rape, murder and an alleged cover-up, invoking IPC Sections 376D, 302, 201, 217, 218 and 120B.Satish Salian had earlier approached the court alleging that his daughter was murdered.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, he said he had provided investigators with the names of people whom he wanted examined.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down,” he said.Asked whether she saw a possible political conspiracy behind the development, Sule did not give a direct answer.“Anything is possible,” she said, while referring to what she called “ICE” — Income Tax, CBI and Enforcement Directorate — and alleging that central agencies had previously been used against political figures who later joined the ruling party.AIMIM leader Waris Pathan, meanwhile, said the case should not be politicised and should be left to the courts.“There is no need to give the Disha Salian case a political colour. There is no need to politicise it,” Pathan said, adding that the matter was sub judice and that “it is best to let the court decide”.Salian’s death had earlier been recorded as an Accidental Death Report. The Bombay High Court had raised concerns over the fact that no FIR was registered despite allegations by her family that she had been murdered.The court also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to her family for years.Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence six days after Salian’s death.The CBI later submitted a closure report in Rajput’s case, concluding that he died by suicide; that report remains pending before the competent court.The Bombay High Court has directed the CBI to investigate the Salian case and has left it to the agency to determine whether a criminal case is made out based on the evidence collected.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian. She said she was surprised because the case had earlier been treated as closed by the same government. AIMIM leader Waris Pathan said the case should not be politicised and should be left to the courts.

Article Title: 'Triumph of truth over jhooth ki goonj': PM Modi hails BJP victory in Rajasthan civic polls
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the state’s municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal corporations.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections,” PM Modi wrote.“This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” he added.PM Modi also congratulated the winning candidates and BJP workers, saying the mandate would strengthen the party’s resolve to work towards development and prosperity in the state.According to figures from the Rajasthan State Election Commission, results for 10,235 of the state’s 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday.The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress. The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.The Congress also recorded a major victory in the Jhalawar municipal council, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.The elections covered 309 urban local bodies — 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipal boards.In Kota Municipal Corporation, the BJP secured 55 of the 100 wards, while Congress won 40 and Independents three. The result for Ward 87 was put on hold after an EVM malfunction.Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma and other party workers staged a protest outside the counting centre, seeking the result and alleging irregularities.Officials later sealed the machine in the presence of the district collector and additional district magistrate and forwarded a report to the Election Commission through the returning officer.The BJP also retained several individual seats. Vivek Rajvanshi won his fourth consecutive term from Ward 54, defeating Congress candidate Manish by 2,226 votes.Gopal Ram Manda secured his fifth consecutive election victory, defeating Congress candidate Sanjay Yadav by 899 votes.Congress and Independent candidates, however, registered victories in some key wards. Youth Congress candidate Arpit Jain defeated BJP veteran and former deputy mayor Yogendra Khinchi by 250 votes in Ward 86.Independent candidate Vandana Faujdar won Ward 71 with 1,264 votes, defeating BJP candidate Meenakshi Sen by 160 votes.In Bundi, the BJP initially emerged as the largest party with 29 wards, two short of a majority. Congress won 20 wards, while Independents secured 11.Later in the day, three Independent candidates, Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar and Vishal Sharma, joined the BJP, taking the party to a majority and enabling it to form the board.The BJP had also captured the previous mid-term board after Congress council chairperson Madu Nuwal was suspended.Congress leaders had expected to retain control but faced criticism over ticket distribution. Former councillors Devraj Gochar, Ankit Buliwal and Jeeshan Ali, who were denied Congress tickets, won as Independents.BJP president Nitin Nabin thanked Rajasthan voters for what he described as a “historic victory”, saying the results showed continued faith in Modi’s leadership.BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also cited the party’s performance in Kota, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had conducted the student-centric programme ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’.“In Kota, where Rahul Gandhi had gone and attempted to create ‘jhooth ki goonj’, the BJP appears to be winning spectacularly,” Trivedi said.He claimed the results demonstrated that the Congress had “more propaganda and less reality” in its claims.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi thanks people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP. Results for 10,235 of the state’s 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday. The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress.

Article Title: Nearly 50 lakh hit by floods in Bihar as swollen rivers breach danger marks
Article Text:
Flood situation worsens in Bihar

Nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of Bihar have been affected by floods as heavy rain in recent days caused rivers already flowing above danger levels to swell further, officials said on Monday.Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.According to the Disaster Management Department, floods have affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts in Bihar.The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, along with heavy rainfall in the state, has pushed several rivers and streams above their danger marks, as cited by PTI.The Ganga was flowing at 36.19 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6.00 pm on Monday, 1.69 metres above the danger level.The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, while the Budhi Gandak had crossed the danger level at Khagaria.The Ganga was above the danger mark at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger. The Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad and Ghaghara at Darauli were also flowing above their respective danger levels.The administration has set up 1,248 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in the flood-hit areas. Around 11,508 people have been provided accommodation, food, medical care and other essential facilities, officials said.The Disaster Management Department said the Gandak barrage at Valmiki Nagar recorded a water discharge of 1,09,000 cusecs at 4 pm on Monday, with the flow continuing to rise.At the Kosi Barrage in Birpur, the discharge stood at 1,63,315 cusecs, against this year's highest flow of 2,55,425 cusecs recorded on July 20.Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 teams of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed across various districts for relief and rescue operations.
Article Summary: Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal. The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai and Munger.

Article Title: UCC in Bihar? JD(U) opposes implementation despite backing Bill in Parliament
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Senior JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak on Monday said the party was opposed to implementing the Uniform Civil Code in Bihar , despite having "supported the UCC Bill" in Parliament.The former JD(U) national general secretary said the party's position on the issue had been clearly articulated by its supreme leader and former chief minister Nitish Kumar "Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said.When asked whether the JD(U)'s position would have little significance with Nitish Kumar stepping down and BJP leader Samrat Choudhary becoming the new chief minister, Rajak strongly rejected the suggestion."The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies... our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he said.When approached for a comment, JD(U) legislature party leader and minister Shrawon Kumar said, "This is an issue on which our spokespersons shall speak. I would like to hear what they say, and then I will say more."Meanwhile, JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha on Monday said party leaders would soon meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in states.“We will soon meet Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the issue,” Jha told news agency PTI.With 12 Lok Sabha MPs, the JD(U) is a key constituent of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and shares power with the BJP in Bihar.The development comes a day after Shah asserted that NDA governments in 21 states would introduce UCC before 2029.Addressing a press conference in Mumbai on Sunday, Shah highlighted the government's initiatives for women and said, “Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced UCC in several states, and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states, we will introduce the UCC before 2029.”The press conference was held to announce a month-long campaign beginning September 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 76th birthday and 25 years of his public service, which began with his tenure as Gujarat chief minister.
Article Summary: Senior JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak on Monday said the party was opposed to implementing the Uniform Civil Code in Bihar. Rajak strongly rejected the suggestion that the party's position would have little significance with Nitish Kumar stepping down and BJP leader Samrat Choudhary becoming the new chief minister.

Article Title: ‘Your collective voice’: Rahul Gandhi invites students to ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ in Indore
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday invited students to join his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ initiative in Indore on September 19, describing it as an opportunity for those “tormented” by the education system to collectively push for change.“I’m coming to Indore on 19 September -- to meet students, to hear you, to talk to you. If you or your loved ones are tormented by the education system and want these conditions to change, you know - ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ is your collective voice, an opportunity to start the change,” Rae Bareli MP said in a post in Hindi on X.He urged students to register through the link shared in his post and join the event in large numbers.“We will discuss in detail every aspect of education and your struggles in Indore,” he said.Former Congress president had last week said India’s education system was failing the generation it was meant to support and asked students, parents and teachers to share why they had lost hope in it.He said fixing the education system should begin by listening to those who experience its problems every day. Rahul had also asked students, parents and teachers to share their experiences, evidence and ideas through an online link.The Indore event will be the fifth edition of the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ initiative. Congress MP has previously held events in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj and Pune.The Pune edition, held on August 22, was focused on girl students.Rahul’s upcoming visit has also triggered a war of words between the Congress and BJP in Madhya Pradesh.Chief minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday took a jibe at Congress leader, calling him “Pappu” while questioning his remarks on the judiciary and armed forces. Yadav also criticised the upcoming Indore event and said Rahul should apologise when he visits the state.Congress leader PC Sharma hit back at the remark, saying, “They kept calling him ‘Pappu’, but now he has become everyone’s ‘Papa’.”BJP leaders subsequently criticised Sharma’s response, with BJP leader Ajay Singh Yadav saying Congress leaders should maintain one narrative.The political exchange comes ahead of Rahul’s September 19 event, where he has said he will engage with students and discuss their concerns about the education system.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi invites students to join his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ initiative in Indore on September 19. He describes it as an opportunity for those ‘tormented’ by the education system to collectively push for change. The event has triggered a war of words between the Congress and BJP in Madhya Pradesh.

Article Title: 'As India leads, world listens': Rajnath Singh hails 18th Brics joint declaration
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh Monday hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly, saying the unison adaptation was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi Calling "inclusive and human-centric approach" an hallmark of the summit, the defence minister laid emphasis on how the bloc put Global South "at the centre, not at the margins, championing a more inclusive, representative and balanced world order"."Rooted in our civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiv Kutumbkam, India has once again shown that leadership is not about having the loudest voice, but the strongest consensus," the Union minister said, adding: "As India leads, the world listens."In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration after intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The talks were complicated by differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia conflict. An earlier meeting of Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had also ended without a joint statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi after a rare meeting between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit.The meeting took place as the conflict continued and helped ease the differences threatening consensus.The declaration used carefully balanced language to address the concerns of both countries. It expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities operating under full International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, describing such actions as violations of international law and relevant IAEA resolutions. The wording amounted to an implicit criticism of US and Israeli strikes on Iran and was important in securing Tehran’s approval.The leaders also recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to maintain the smooth movement of global trade, supply chains and energy in line with international law.Official sources said India conducted prolonged negotiations at several levels to bridge the differences between Iran and the UAE. Other member-states also supported the effort, keen to ensure that the summit ended with a joint declaration rather than another failure to reach consensus.The agreement recalled the last-minute G20 declaration adopted in New Delhi in 2023 during the Russia-Ukraine war. That statement used carefully worded language urging countries not to use force to seize territory without directly naming Russia.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh hailed New Delhi Brics declaration passed unanimosly. Singh said it was an "statement of India’s growing global influence" under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In a dramatic echo of the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi, Brics countries agreed on a joint declaration.

Article Title: MPSC paper leak: CJP to join protesters demanding resignation of key officials, sets Sept 24 deadline
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke, the party founder, confirmed his backing after engaging with the aspiring candidates

CJP threatens statewide tour

Abhijeet Dipke backs MPSC aspirants' demands





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) and its founder Abhijeet Dipke will join MPSC aspirants protesting alleged paper leaks and irregularities in online examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission, the party said on Sunday.The CJP has also set a September 24 deadline for its demand seeking the resignation of the MPSC chairman and secretary.The announcement followed a meeting between a group of MPSC aspirants and Dipke at his residence in the Waluj area of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The CJP said the agitation demanding the resignation of the MPSC chairman and secretary would continue.If the two officials did not step down by September 24, Dipke and party members would undertake a statewide tour to meet MPSC aspirants and take up their concerns, the party said in a release.Dipke and other CJP members will also participate in the ongoing protests by MPSC aspirants, it said.After meeting the aspirants, Dipke said in a video message, "The CJP and I are with MPSC aspirants in this fight. We will stand with the aspirants till the resignations (of top MPSC officials)."MPSC aspirants have held protests at several places across Maharashtra , seeking greater transparency in the recruitment process and action over alleged paper leaks and other irregularities in various examinations conducted by the commission.The protests have centred on demands for accountability and transparency in the conduct of MPSC examinations.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party and its founder Abhijeet Dipke will join MPSC aspirants protesting alleged paper leaks and irregularities in online examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission. The CJP has also set a September 24 deadline for its demand seeking the resignation of the M PSC chairman and secretary.

Article Title: ‘29 Sept tak metro mein safar na karein’: Multiple Delhi schools receive bomb threats
Article Text:
The emails reportedly claimed that blasts would target courts and police stations in the national capital (File photo)





NEW DELHI: Several schools in Delhi received bomb threats via email on Tuesday, prompting security checks and searches across the affected premises.The threat email, reportedly sent in Punjabi, claimed that blasts would target courts and police stations in the national capital.The threat emails were received at around 10:17 am. The schools named among those affected include Air Force Bal Bharati School (AFBBS), Carmel Convent School and The British School.One of the threat emails carried the subject line: “B00000M|B New Dellhi Schools @ 1:11PM.”The email contained threatening messages, including: “Delhi BanayGa KHALISTAN” and “School @1:11pm Delhi valio Apne Bachay Bachao Koi ve Metro Yan Traina Vich 29 Sept Tak Safar na Karna, Delhi da har police thana Nishana iPhone Dhamake hon Ge.”The email further threatened court premises, stating: “Court @3:11pm Tees Hazari, Karkardoma Court, Patila Court Khalistan vale Sikhan Nu jhoothe case Saja karde - Ajj ton courtan te parkng Vich Lagatar Scooterian Nal Dhamake.”It also warned: “Delhi da har police chowkian Nishane te,” according to the email.Following the threats, a major security operation was launched at the affected schools. Delhi Police deployed bomb disposal squads and sniffer dog units to conduct thorough searches of the premises.Multiple fire tenders and ambulances were kept on standby as a precautionary measure. Sniffer dogs searched classrooms, corridors and open areas, while personnel from the bomb detection and disposal squads scanned the premises using specialised equipment for any possible explosive devices.Local police personnel were also deployed to manage crowds of concerned parents and maintain security around the schools.
Article Summary: The threat email, reportedly sent in Punjabi, claimed that blasts would target courts and police stations in the national capital. The schools named among those affected include Air Force Bal Bharati School (AFBBS), Carmel Convent School and The British School.

Article Title: 'Was laughing': Video shows Indian-origin woman, friend moments before NYC subway train ran over them
Article Text:
An Indian origin woman and her friend were tragically hit by a subway train in NYC.

What happened on the tracks?

Why were they on the tracks?

Who were Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul?

Indian-origin woman and her friend, both 24-year-old, from New Jersey were fatally struck by a New York City subway train early Sunday after they were seen sitting on the tracks at a Manhattan station. Investigators are trying to determine how and why they ended up in the path of the approaching train.Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul, both recent Rutgers University graduates, were on the tracks at Spring Street station in Lower Manhattan shortly after 3 am when a southbound No 4 train entered the station. The train operator saw the pair and tried to stop, but was unable to prevent the collision. Both were pronounced dead at the scene. Around 100 passengers were later evacuated from the train, according to reports.The circumstances surrounding the deaths remain unclear. Investigators are examining whether Kaul first fell or went onto the tracks and Chitre followed in an attempt to help him, whether intoxication played a role, or whether the possibility of suicide should be considered.An incident report obtained by the New York Daily News said the train operator told supervisors that she saw the man and woman sitting on the tracks as the train approached.She attempted to stop the train, but it was too late.The report said Chitre appeared to be laughing and pulling Kaul towards her when the train struck them. Separately, law-enforcement sources told the New York Post that Kaul may have fallen or made his way onto the tracks before Chitre went down after him.Video circulating on social media also appeared to show the pair sitting together on the tracks shortly before the train arrived. AmNewYork reported that the operator activated the emergency brake but could not stop the train in time.The medical examiner has not yet released an official determination explaining the circumstances of the deaths.One possibility being examined is that Kaul ended up on the tracks first and Chitre went down to help him.Police sources told the New York Post that it was not immediately clear whether Kaul had fallen or climbed down. Chitre appeared to try to pull him towards her before the train hit them.If that account is confirmed, Chitre may have gone onto the tracks in an attempt to rescue her friend, rather than intentionally placing herself in the path of the train.However, investigators have not established what happened immediately before the pair were seen on the tracks.Investigators are also looking into whether one or both of them were intoxicated and may have been too impaired or disoriented to recognise the danger posed by the approaching train, according to law-enforcement sources.The footage showing the pair apparently remaining on the tracks as the train approached has raised questions about whether they understood what was happening around them. But there has been no official finding that alcohol or drugs were involved, and toxicology results, if any, have not been made public.Suicide has also been posed as a possible explanation.No suicide note was found at the scene, according to sources cited by the New York Post. However, the absence of a note does not by itself establish how the pair came to be on the tracks, and investigators have not concluded that their deaths were intentional.At present, there is no publicly established motive for why the two were on the tracks.Chitre and Kaul were longtime friends who attended Rutgers University around the same time and graduated in 2024.Chitre, from the Dayton section of South Brunswick, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers with a degree in public health and a minor in business administration. She was working as a quality operations specialist at pharmaceutical company Acadia Pharmaceuticals and had recently begun pursuing a Doctor of Pharmacy degree at Temple University.Kaul, from Sayreville, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers Business School with a degree in finance. He had been working as a financial data analyst at Bloomberg since 2025.The two were part of the same social circles and South Asian community around Rutgers, according to people who knew them. Rajnikant Pipalia, whose son was a close friend of Kaul, told the New York Post that the pair had grown up in the same social world and remained part of the same wider group of friends.Their deaths came as they were beginning their professional lives.
Article Summary: Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul, both 24, were on the tracks at Spring Street station in Lower Manhattan when a southbound No 4 train entered the station. The train operator saw the pair and tried to stop, but was unable to prevent the collision. Investigators are trying to determine how and why they ended up in the path of the approaching train.

Article Title: Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales sign historic MoU to break away from UK
Article Text:
Scottish first minister John Swinney, his Welsh counterpart Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill signed the MoU at a summit in Cardiff.

LONDON: Elected representatives of three devolved UK legislatures – Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales – signed a historic pact on Monday, declaring their intent to break free of Westminster’s control.“The political landscape across these islands is changing. For the first time ever, there are first ministers in Scotland, in Wales and in the North of Ireland who are all committed to independence from the United Kingdom. For people watching around the world, there could be no clearer sign that Westminster’s time is coming to an end,” states the MoU.Scottish first minister John Swinney, his Welsh counterpart Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill signed the MoU at a summit in Cardiff. Sinn Fein president Mary Lou McDonald, leader of the opposition in Ireland, was the fourth signatory.“Our nations have the right to self-determination: No Westminster govt has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future,” says the MoU.Plaid Cymru’s victory at the Senedd (Welsh parliament) elections in May ended Labour’s unbroken control of the Welsh govt since devolution began in 1999.It meant that the largest parties in all three devolved parliaments of the UK were pro-independence for the first time.“Each of our nations has the right to determine its own future, through democratic means and in accordance with the wishes of its people. We call for the British govt to prepare for, plan and facilitate constitutional change in each jurisdiction,” the agreement states.The MoU commits the parties to strengthening cooperation in areas such as the economy and energy resources, backed by a consensus that the future of these nations belongs in the European Union.UK PM Andy Burnham believes strongly in the UK and is focused on easing the cost-of-living crisis rather than on “constitutional debates”, Downing Street said.Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross described the meeting as “a separatist summit” and “performative photo call”.
Article Summary: Scottish first minister John Swinney, his Welsh counterpart Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill signed the MoU. Sinn Fein president Mary Lou McDonald, leader of the opposition in Ireland, was the fourth signatory.

Article Title: ‘It was intentional’: Biker Siya’s father seeks attempt to murder charge against Gurgaon car driver
Article Text:
Biker Sia's father

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think social media is an effective way for victims to seek justice? Yes, it raises awareness. No, it may complicate legal processes. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GURGAON: The father of biker Siya, whose video alleging a hit-and-run on Golf Course Road went viral, said he learnt about the incident only an hour earlier and would have filed an FIR himself had he known about it.Speaking to the media, Siya’s father said, “I only found out about the accident an hour ago. Otherwise, I would have gone and filed an FIR myself”.Also read more: ‘They are playing victim card’: Accused Kalyan Bainsla denies deliberate hit, blames biker in Gurgaon crash “It wasn’t even night; it happened during the day,” Siya’s father added.“We are fortunate that our daughter wasn’t hurt. I asked her, ‘If such an incident happened, why didn’t you tell us? You should have told us when you got home,” Siya’s father further added.Speaking to the media, brother of victim Siya said, “The incident happened yesterday morning. We hadn’t told our parents at home, though they sensed something had happened to her."" She had initially attributed her discomfort to body pain from the gym. She had called me first when the accident occurred. She told me there had been an accident. At first, I thought she had slipped. Then she explained that it was a hit-and-run.Someone had been chasing her and making abusive gestures," Siya's brother added." You must have seen the video; she was signalling them to keep their distance. Yet, they rolled down their window and made very offensive gestures. There were four people in the vehicle, and all of them were drunk. She told me this. This happened between 7:30 and 8:00am ," Siya's brother said."The men had likely been out drinking since the night before and encountered her on the road in the morning. She is experiencing something akin to trauma. Regarding the FIR registered in Gurugram, our lawyer has spoken to the SHO there about further action. We will also be filing an FIR on our own behalf," Siya's brother further added.According to Siya said, she would file an FIR with her lawyer by Monday evening and take legal action in the matter.In an Instagram story, Siya thanked people for their support and said she had seen efforts being made to identify the person involved in the incident. She also said she was receiving requests from news channels and journalists for interviews but would not be speaking to the media.“I do not wish to reveal my identity or face, and I won't be giving any interviews this time,” Siya said, asking people to respect her decision.She added that she would keep them updated and asked those seeking more information to contact her through Instagram.Sia had earlier shared a video recorded on an action camera mounted on her motorcycle, alleging that a car repeatedly followed her while she was riding with a group of bikers on Sunday before hitting her motorcycle and fleeing.She alleged that the occupants appeared to be intoxicated and that the driver asked her to stop despite her asking him to maintain a safe distance. She said she continued riding ahead as she felt the situation was unsafe.The footage appears to show the car coming into contact with her motorcycle, knocking her off the bike and dragging the motorcycle for several metres before fleeing.Siya said one of her friends chased the car and confronted the driver at a traffic signal. According to her, the driver denied responsibility and drove away.The car owner, Manish, has since said the vehicle belonged to him but had been borrowed by his friend Kalyan Singh two days earlier. Manish said he was at work and learnt about the accident only on Monday morning. He said Singh did not answer his calls when he tried to contact him.Gurgaon Police has taken suo motu cognisance of the viral video and said the accused would be identified and arrested at the earliest. Police are registering a case under relevant sections at Sector 56 police station.
Article Summary: Siya's father says he only found out about the accident an hour ago. He said he would have filed an FIR himself had he known about it. Siya said she would file an FIR with her lawyer by Monday evening. She thanked people for their support and said she had seen efforts being made to identify the person.

Article Title: 3 UP youths missing in Russia; told kin ‘forced to fight against Ukraine’
Article Text:
While UP authorities assured families of inquiries and assistance, relatives await their safe repatriation.

(With inputs from Sudeep Lavania in Agra and Sachin Sharma in Shamli)





AGRA/SHAMLI: Amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict, families of three young men from western Uttar Pradesh are living in despair after losing contact with their sons in Moscow.The youths, who travelled to Russia on study visas last year, reportedly claimed before going silent that local authorities confiscated their passports and forced them into military service.The missing youths are Himanshu Sharma (24) and Shakti Punder (23), both from Muzaffarnagar, and Ashu Saini (25) from Shamli district. The three men were sharing a room in the Russian capital Moscow and were pursuing a Russian language course.According to relatives, the last contact with the students came on July 30, when brief phone calls were made before their lines went dead and their phones switched off. Himanshu Sharma went to Russia on a student visa to study and take up permissible part-time work.His cousin, Priyanshu Sharma, told reporters, “His passport was due to expire this year. Since that last call on July 30, we have called his number several times with no response. We suspect he could be forced into the Russian Army.”Similarly, Shakti Punder’s father reported speaking to him last on the same day, after which all communication ceased.Ashu Saini hailed from Hasanpur Lohari village in Shamli’s Thanabhawan area and left for Russia in April 2026.His sister, Anshul, recalled a hurried 30-second final conversation where he briefly mentioned he was fine before hanging up.Ashu’s father, Rakesh Kumar, a farmer, has formally appealed to the Prime Minister’s Office seeking his son’s safe return.Following desperate pleas from the families, appeals were dispatched to ministry of external affairs (MEA). In response, MEA informed the families that India’s embassy in Moscow has actively intervened.“The embassy has taken up the matter with the Russian authorities concerned. They have reportedly joined the Russian army; the embassy has sought details of their whereabouts. The embassy is separately taking up their case,” the MEA stated in its reply to the families of the youths.In July, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal acknowledged that approximately 24 Indian citizens—recruited through fraudulent or non-transparent means—remain stuck serving within the ranks of Russian army as the war in Ukraine persists.While local authorities in Uttar Pradesh have assured grieving families that inquiries are underway and assistance will be extended, relatives continue to wait anxiously for their safe repatriation.
Article Summary: The youths, who travelled to Russia on study visas last year, reportedly claimed before going silent that local authorities confiscated their passports and forced them into military service. The missing youths are Himanshu Sharma (24) and Shakti Punder (23) from Muzaffarnagar, and Ashu Saini (25) from Shamli district.

Article Title: Manoj Jarange changes tack, plans ‘solo’ march into Mumbai
Article Text:
Jarange, who has been on an indefinite fast at Antarwali Sarati since Aug 29, said he would leave for Mumbai on Tuesday





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Monday altered his Mumbai agitation plan, saying he would travel to the city with just four to five associates. Jarange took this decision after police denied permission for his proposed hunger strike at Azad Maidan during Ganeshotsav.The move came even as chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed to Jarange to reconsider travelling to Mumbai during the festival and said most of his demands had already been addressed.“Almost all demands have been met. Some demands are in court and at different stages. But demands cannot be met unless one approaches the court or another constitutional forum. We have apprised him about it,” Fadnavis told reporters in Mumbai.Jarange, who has been on an indefinite fast at Antarwali Sarati since Aug 29, said he would leave for Mumbai on Tuesday and reach the state capital on Sept 19 via Patoda, Shrigonda, Hadapsar and Khopoli.“If I am stopped, lakhs of Marathas will enter Mumbai without permission,” he warned. Mumbai Police have reportedly informed Jarange that permission for his hunger strike could be considered after Ganeshotsav and at a venue other than Azad Maidan.It is the second consecutive rejection of permission for the agitation.Seeking Kunbi recognition for the entire Maratha community and reservation benefits under the OBC quota, Jarange said he would first “fight the battle alone.” He urged supporters not to use the vehicles and funds collected for the agitation.Jarange also said he had stopped taking saline and that the next few days would be “life-threatening”. He added that he would spend nights in public places rather than at private residences along the route.Minister Shambhuraj Desai said he would soon meet Jarange to clear what he termed misunderstandings. He said some of Jarange’s statements were “half-truths” and that govt was sincerely pursuing legal processes on issues such as the Satara Gazette and 58 lakh Kunbi records.Shiv Sena politician Ramdas Kadam also appealed to Jarange to exercise restraint during Ganeshotsav, claiming that 14 of his demands had been accepted and the remaining issues were under consideration. He said govt’s position that justice for the Maratha community should not come at the cost of the OBC community is appropriate.Meanwhile, BJP state president Chandrashekhar Bawankule, without naming Jarange, urged all organisations and individuals to avoid protests during Ganeshotsav and help maintain social harmony.
Article Summary: Jarange took this decision after police denied permission for his proposed hunger strike at Azad Maidan during Ganeshotsav. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed to Jarange to reconsider travelling to Mumbai during the festival and said most of his demands had already been addressed. Jarange has been on an indefinite fast at Antarwali Sarati since Aug 29.

Article Title: West Bengal shunts IPS officer days after complaint by ‘Hindu Legal Fund’
Article Text:
The transfer comes days after a video she posted encouraging UPSC aspirants drew criticism on social media.





KOLKATA: IPS officer Bushra Bano, additional SP, Kharagpur, was transferred on Monday as deputy commandant of the state armed police.The transfer comes days after a video she posted encouraging UPSC aspirants drew criticism on social media.In the Sept 13 video, Bano, an IPS officer of the 2021 batch, spoke about how Aligarh Muslim University ’s Residential Coaching Academy helped her prepare for the UPSC.Several X users criticised her for not using “Jai Hind” or “Vande Mataram”.An X handle — Hindu Legal Fund — said it had complained to the Bengal home secretary over the video. It alleged: “She began with Assalamualaikum, used Inshallah, ended with Jazakallah—and did not use Vande Mataram or Jai Hind. A serving officer representing the Indian state should maintain neutrality and use national expressions in public communication. Seeking appropriate review and action.”The govt also transferred Partha Ghosh as additional SP, Kharagpur, and Subhendu Mondal as additional DC, Chandannagar Police Commissionerate.
Article Summary: Bushra Bano, additional SP, Kharagpur, was transferred on Monday as deputy commandant of the state armed police. The transfer comes days after a video she posted encouraging UPSC aspirants drew criticism on social media. In the Sept 13 video, Bano spoke about how Aligarh Muslim University ’s Residential Coaching Academy helped her prepare for the UPSC.

Article Title: Gym trainer shot dead in south Delhi; cops suspect rivalry that has claimed 2 lives
Article Text:
Ritu Lohia (R), inconsolable after her husband's killing, is embraced by a relative inside her home in Aya Nagar

South Delhi gym trainer murder





NEW DELHI: A 32-year-old gym trainer was shot dead after bike-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at him in south Delhi ’s Fatehpur Beri on Monday morning.Police suspect the attack may be linked to an old rivalry between two families that has already claimed two lives in the past. No arrests have been made yet.The victim, identified as Vijay Kumar , was a resident of Fatehpur Beri. He is survived by his 24-year-old wife.The incident took place around 10am near Hansa Chowk when Vijay was working at the gym. According to sources, four men were involved in the attack and were lying in wait for him outside.The suspects, wearing helmets, were on two motorcycles that allegedly had fake number plates, said a source. However, police said only two men were involved in the attack. “It appears they had been conducting reconnaissance for the past few days,” said the source.Vijay was called outside the gym by a person on the pretext that someone wanted to speak to him. He was ambushed the minute he stepped out, with the assailants firing about 12-15 rounds.Vijay suffered multiple injuries on different parts of his body, including at least two in the head.He was taken to a hospital, where he was declared dead.Deputy commissioner of police (south) Anant Mittal said a team rushed to the spot on receiving information about the firing. “Several rounds were fired by two suspects, resulting in one person sustaining fatal injuries and subsequently succumbing,” he said.An FIR was registered under BNS Section 103 (murder) at Fatehpuri Beri police station against unknown persons. Raids are being conducted at various locations to trace the suspects and multiple teams have been formed to identify and arrest them, Mittal said.Vijay’s uncle Narender Lohmod claimed that one of the attackers hails from the same village. The family suspects the murder could be linked to an old rivalry with another family from a village in Fatehpur Beri. Police are probing a possible link, and also if the Randeep Bhati-Neeraj Faridpuriya gang is involved. “The motive seems to arise from personal enmity,” said Mittal.According to the family, the rivalry dates back to 2024, when Deepak, a friend of Vijay’s brother Ajay, was allegedly attacked in connection with a long-standing dispute over a plot. An attempt-to-murder case was subsequently registered against 24-year-old businessman Arun Lohia, who was the prime suspect.The dispute escalated in May 2025, when Deepak and his associates allegedly opened fire on an SUV near Chhatarpur metro station, killing Lohia while he was returning home with his father. Lohia’s father later claimed 20-25 rounds were fired in the attack. Police arrested three people, including Deepak and Ajay, in connection with the case.On Nov 30, Deepak’s father Ratan Lohiya, a dairy businessman, was shot dead near his home when he was on his way to his dairy in Aya Nagar. The family alleged nearly 70 rounds were fired at him.Vijay’s family alleged he was targeted by the businessman’s family despite having no connection with the earlier incidents. “He had no involvement in the dispute. He had been living and working peacefully,” Lohmod said.
Article Summary: Vijay Kumar, 32, shot dead after bike-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at him in south Delhi. Police suspect the attack may be linked to an old rivalry between two families that has already claimed two lives in the past. The victim, identified as Vijay Kumar, was a resident of Fatehpur Beri.

Article Title: 'Even Donald Trump is copying us': DK Shivakumar says US $5,000 promise 'inspired' by Congress guarantees
Article Text:
Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar stated Donald Trump is copying Congress's guarantee schemes





BENGALURU: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Monday said even US President Donald Trump was “copying” the Congress government ’s guarantee schemes, while highlighting what he described as their popularity among people.Speaking in Bengaluru, Shivakumar said the Congress government’s welfare guarantees had become a “blockbuster” and drew a comparison with Trump’s recent promise to give every adult American $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in the November midterm elections.Trump has renewed his proposal for a $5,000 “dividend” for every adult American, saying the US government could afford the payments because it was collecting large amounts of revenue.“I don't know but it's easy if the Republicans win. $5,000 to all adults in the country and we can easily handle that because we're taking in so much money,” Trump told reporters in Ireland on Sunday, according to reports.Trump had first unveiled the proposal at a Republican Party convention in Dallas. He linked the proposed payments to what he described as trillions of dollars flowing into the US.
Article Summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said even US President Donald Trump was “copying’ the Congress government’s guarantee schemes. Shivak Kumar drew a comparison with Trump's recent promise to give every adult American $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate.

Article Title: ‘Fake turbans’ vs ‘insult to Gurus, people’: Bhagwant Mann, Nayab Saini trade barbs
Article Text:
Reacting to it, Saini called Mann’s statement “extremely unfortunate” and hit back.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and his Haryana counterpart, Nayab Singh Saini, traded barbs over the turban at separate press conferences on Monday.It all began when Mann, during a presser, sought to suggest that Saini had a "ready-to-wear turban" in his car which he put on for visits to Punjab, while emphasising that Saini could not win hearts of Punjabis by placing “fake turbans (nakli pagaan)” on his head.In the evening, during a press conference at Punjab BJP headquarters, Saini termed Mann’s remarks “nakli pagg (fake turban)” “an insult to the people of Punjab” and asked Mann to apologise to the people and the Sikh Gurus, who adorned the dastaar (turban).Earlier in the day, Mann said, “Saini sahib doesn’t really understand these things. They simply put a turban on him and send him here. He thinks that once the photo is taken, the job is done.”Taking the swipe further, Mann said, “He keeps a turban in his car. Sometimes, he is in Panchkula and comes to Punjab wearing that turban. Ona nu eh lagda ki edan nakli pagaan dhar ke shaayad Punjabiyan da dil jit lainge. Edan ho nai sakda (He thinks that by placing these fake turbans, perhaps they will win the hearts of Punjabis. That won’t happen).”Reacting to it, Saini called Mann’s statement “extremely unfortunate” and hit back."The turban is a symbol of respect for the Gurus. It represents a person’s self-respect and dignity. The Gurus placed this dastaar on their heads. If Mann sahib is calling it a ‘fake turban’, he should go to that sacred place where the Gurus adorned this dastaar and apologise. He should apologise to the people of Punjab as well. The sangat is considered the Guru itself and if he has called it a ‘fake turban’, then he has insulted the people of Punjab. He should apologise to the people of Punjab,” he added.Saini has been a frequent visitor to Punjab, highlighting the works carried out by BJP-ruled Haryana and simultaneously slamming AAP’s governance in Punjab. Promising to replicate the Haryana governance model in Punjab while seeking support for BJP, Saini has been urging people to bring “a double engine” govt in Punjab in the 2027 elections.On Monday, Saini was late by an hour and a half to a scheduled news conference at Punjab BJP headquarters in Chandigarh in connection with the joining of Major Bhupinder Singh Dhillon, a relative of former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal. He apologised to the waiting media and said he got late for the news conference due to an event in Delhi. Major Dhillon, who served as political secretary to former CM Badal, eventually joined BJP, in the presence of Saini, Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon and other party leadership. Responding to a question on the possibility of an alliance with the SAD, Saini said, “Our alliance is with the people of Punjab.”
Article Summary: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and his Haryana counterpart Nayab Singh Saini traded barbs over the turban at separate press conferences on Monday. It all began when Mann, during a presser, sought to suggest that Sainsi had a "ready-to-wear turban" in his car. Mann emphasised that Saintsi could not win hearts of Punjabis by placing “fake turbans (nakli pagaan)” on his head.

Article Title: 'Head down with shame': Sonam Wangchuk says LG’s compensation for Sept 24 victims small
Article Text:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk says LG’s compensation for Sept 24 victims small (PTI photo)





SRINAGAR: A day after Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena announced compensation for victims of the September 24 violence, in which four people were killed in alleged police firing and scores of others injured, Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said was unhappy with the “small” compensation amount and his “head is down with shame.”In his social media post, Wangchuk on Monday evening said that “Looking at this compensation, I do not feel happy, rather my head is down with shame,” Wangchuk said.On Sunday evening the LG Ladakh said, “in our continued commitment to support the families affected by the tragic violence in Ladakh on 24 September last year, today sanctioned a compensation of Rs 15 lakh to the next of kin of each of the four deceased. An ex-gratia of Rs 3 lakh for those with major injuries and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries has also been approved.”“While no compensation amount can replace a life lost or erase the pain endured, the Ladakh Administration firmly stands beside every affected family in their journey towards healing and overcoming the grief,” LG Ladakh said.However, Wangchuk said “you can see that the families of those who died have been offered Rs 15 lakh, while those who were injured and remain disabled for the rest of their lives are offered Rs 3 lakh.”Wangchuk said most of these people were “unarmed civilians and walking on the road” when they were fired upon. “They were shot in the head, chest and legs and that too without any firing order,” Wangchuk claimed. “There was no order to open fire, still AK-47 rifles were used against them,” he alleged.He said that the truth would have come out if the report of the inquiry commission set up to investigate the incident had been released. “Instead, that report is being suppressed. It has been a year and the truth is still not being revealed.”The LAB member said that the country must stand with Ladakh as among “those who lost their lives were former soldiers.” “During the Kargil War, some of them were injured and brought down from the mountains to hospitals. After recovering, they could have returned home but instead they chose to go back and fight for the country. Such people were shot from behind and dragged,” Wangchuk alleged“I will continue to share these stories and facts one by one if proper compensation and justice are not provided. In the interest of the nation, I have remained silent until now. But if such treatment is meted out to people who displayed such courage and sacrifice, then the truth must be placed before the country, whether or not the inquiry commission's report is ever released,” Wangchuk said.On September 24 2025, police allegedly opened fire on protesters demanding Sixth Schedule status and statehood for Ladakh after demonstrations turned violent, killing four people and injuring nearly 90. Following the violence, authorities in Leh imposed curfew-like restrictions, suspended mobile internet and arrested over 80 people with FIR registered against 87. Following the incident the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance, two major political groupings refused to have talks with the centre until a judicial commission was announced.Then on October 17 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs announced a judicial probe headed by a Dr Justice B S Chauhan (former judge, Supreme Court of India) to probe into the September 24 violence in Leh making it a major outreach to the region after weeks of unrest and tension. Retired district and sessions judge Mohan Singh Parihar is its judicial secretary. The commission began its work on October 27 2025. However, the commission is yet to submit its report.After the announcement of the judicial commission, the centre held talks with representatives of the LAB and the KDA on October 22 in New Delhi. Since then Chering Dorjay Lakrook, LAB co-chairman says that LAB has raised the issue of September 24 firing and compensation for the victims in every meeting with the MHA.After the September 9, 2026 meeting in New Delhi, the Ladakh groups said the centre has assured to withdraw cases against those arrested in September 2025 and provide compensation to victims and injured.
Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk says LG’s compensation for Sept 24 victims small. Wangchuk said most of these people were “unarmed civilians and walking on the road” when they were fired upon. “They were shot in the head, chest and legs and that too without any firing order,” Wangchuk claimed.

Article Title: 4 of a family killed after refrigerator explodes in Belagavi house
Article Text:
A refrigerator explosion and subsequent fire tragically killed four family members in Belagavi





BELAGAVI: Four members of a family were killed and two others critically injured after a refrigerator reportedly exploded and triggered a fire at their house in Chavat Galli, near the Central Bus Stand, late on Monday night.The fire engulfed the house within minutes, trapping the occupants inside and leaving them with little chance to escape. The incident occurred while the family was observing Ganesh Chaturthi, shocking residents in the area.The deceased have been identified as Gajanan Damone, 65; Sharada Damone, 45; Bharati Damone, 50; and Roshan Damone, 21.Priya Damone, 28, and Ganga Damone, 25, suffered serious injuries and were shifted to a hospital, where they are undergoing treatment.The incident has left the family’s relatives devastated, particularly as it occurred during the festival celebrations. The fire broke out within the limits of the Market police station.The exact cause of the refrigerator explosion and the subsequent fire is yet to be established. Police are investigating the incident.
Article Summary: Four members of a family were killed and two others critically injured after a refrigerator reportedly exploded and triggered a fire. The incident occurred while the family was observing Ganesh Chaturthi, shocking residents in the area. The exact cause of the refrigerator explosion and the subsequent fire is yet to be established.

Article Title: Ram Temple Ceo: Temple care is matter of duty forme, not publicity: Ram temple CEO
Article Text:
Jeetendra Mishra, the newly appointed CEO, passionately defended his extensive experience in temple administration, highlighting his management of over 50 religious sites throughout his Air Force career.





LUCKNOW: Responding to questions being raised in social media over his suitability to oversee the work of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, newly appointed CEO and retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra asserted that temple administration has long been part of his responsibilities and dismissed criticism of his background.Mishra said that during his tenure as Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Air Command, more than 50 sarva dharm sthals located at Air Force bases from Rajasthan to Ladakh were under his patronage.“I have looked after each of them,” he said, adding that managing these pious places was a matter of duty rather than public recognition.Rejecting allegations that a military officer may lack experience in temple affairs, Mishra said his association with temple management was discussed during the CEO selection process. He told the panel that several temples had functioned under his oversight during his Air Force career.“Looking after a temple is my dharma. I don’t go to the media telling them that I am looking after a temple,” Mishra said. He added that seeking publicity for such work reflected a flawed mindset.The retired Air Marshal also highlighted his visits to major pilgrimage centres, including Kedarnath, Rameswaram, Guruvayur and Padmanabhaswamy Temple, while maintaining that religious faith remains a personal matter.Mishra was selected for the top post after a competitive process involving 16 candidates from the IAS, IPS, armed forces and other services.Trust sources told TOI that Mishra visited Ayodhya for the interview on August 10 and after giving face to face interview with selection committee left for Delhi on August 12. During his two-day stay in Ayodhya, he was provided accommodation and also visited Shree Ram Lalla temple for darshan.Positioning his experience as both administrative and spiritual, Mishra said his Air Force journey began with a visit to a temple and concluded with a pilgrimage to Kedarnath.Mishra was among 16 candidates interviewed for the CEO post. The candidates included Ajit Kesari, a retired IAS officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre who served as additional chief secretary; Dr Paresh Saxena, a 1994-batch Bihar-cadre IPS officer; Shubhranshu Mani, former principal chief mechanical engineer of the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) and a key member of the team that designed and manufactured Train 18, which later became the Vande Bharat Express; Gopal Krishna Dwivedi, special chief secretary in the Andhra Pradesh government who has also served with the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD); Col Dr Harindra Tripathi, registrar of IIM Guwahati; Lt Gen (retired) Ajai Kumar Sahgal, consultant with Bharat Dynamics Limited; Kamal Kant Sharma, retired DG of CRPF; and Major General Sanjay Pratapsingh Vishwasrao.The list also included retired Air Marshal Amit Tiwari, formerly associated with Central Air Command and instrumental in the development of the Kaveri engine for the Tejas programme and the Agni missile programme; Dr Dinesh Chandra Mishra, retired special secretary in the PWD; and Shruti Bhardwaj, a 2013-batch promoted IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre who is currently on extension.The other four candidates were former IPS officer Rajesh Kumar Pandey, retired Major General Rajiv Chhibber of the Dogra Regiment, retired Brigadier Satyendra Prasad Sinha and retired Major General Ajay Kumar Sharma.
Article Summary: Jeetendra Mishra was selected for the top post after a competitive process involving 16 candidates from the IAS, IPS, armed forces and other services. The retired Air Marshal highlighted his visits to major pilgrimage centres, including Kedarnath, Rameswaram and Guruvayur.

Article Title: ‘Drunk men made offensive gestures, she is experiencing trauma’: Gurgaon biker’s brother
Article Text:
Abhishek Chauhan, advocate of victim Sia, said that she somehow managed to get home.

(With agency inputs)





GURGAON: The family of the woman whose two-wheeler was “hit from behind by a car” on Gurgaon’s Golf Course Road on Sunday morning said they would file a police complaint through her brother, alleging that there were “four drunk people in the vehicle”. The family said she is “experiencing something akin to trauma”.Gurgaon Police had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of the Golf Course Road incident in which a viral video showed a four-wheeler hitting a woman two-wheeler rider from behind.The Police have registered an FIR against the accused car driver.Sia’s brother said the incident happened on Sunday morning and that they did not inform their parents about it. He said his sister initially did not tell them about the incident, but later informed them that it was a hit-and-run case. He said someone had been chasing her and making abusive gestures.Sia's brother also said her sister told the people in the four-wheeler to keep their distance but they "made offensive gestures"."We hadn't told our parents at home, though they sensed something had happened to her. She had initially attributed her discomfort to body pain from the gym.She had called me first when the accident occurred. She told me there had been an accident. At first, I thought she had slipped. Then she explained that it was a hit-and-run. Someone had been chasing her and making abusive gestures," he told news agency ANI."You must have seen the video; she was signalling them to keep their distance. Yet, they rolled down their window and made very offensive gestures. There were four people in the vehicle, and all of them were drunk. She told me this. This happened between 7:30 and 8:00 AM. The men had likely been out drinking since the night before and encountered her on the road in the morning. She is experiencing something akin to trauma. Regarding the FIR registered in Gurgaon, our lawyer has spoken to the SHO there about further action. We will also be filing an FIR on our own behalf," he added.The victim’s father said they would have filed a police complaint had they known about the incident earlier."I only found out about the accident an hour ago. Otherwise, I would have gone and filed an FIR myself. It wasn't even night; it happened during the day. We are fortunate that our daughter wasn't hurt. I asked her, 'If such an incident happened, why didn't you tell us? You should have told us when you got home," he said.Abhishek Chauhan, advocate of victim Sia, said that she somehow managed to get home."We are going to file a complaint now. She told me about the incident-it happened yesterday morning. There were four guys in a car who were drunk. They had tried to tease her earlier; she gestured for them to move aside-you can see this in the video-telling them to back off. Then, as they drove past, they sideswiped her vehicle and sped away. The incident took place near Golf Course Road in Gurgaon," he said."She somehow managed to get home, and once she arrived, she shared the details with me. I am on my way to file the complaint right now. The Motor Vehicles Act will apply, as well as the BNS," he added.Gurgaon Police had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of the Golf Course Road incident.The FIR was registered at Sector 56 police station in Gurgaon after the police’s Social Media Monitoring Cell spotted the video circulating on social media on September 14.Gurgaon Police had earlier said that no written complaint had been received from the victim and that they initiated action after taking cognisance of the viral video."On September 14, our Social Media Monitoring Cell intercepted a video showing a four-wheeler hitting a female two-wheeler rider from behind. This incident occurred on Golf Course Road; the Gurgaon Police have contacted the woman involved and, taking suo motu cognisance, have registered an FIR at the Sector 56 Police Station in Gurgaon," Gurgaon assistant commissioner of police (ACP) Abhilaksh Joshi told ANI earlier."We are monitoring instances of rash or negligent driving and any such incidents occurring in Gurgaon. Even without a formal complaint, we will take suo motu cognisance and initiate action in accordance with the law; our special cell, created specifically for this purpose, is also keeping a close watch. People should not get involved in such incidents, nor should they spread baseless rumours about them. Doing so is a legal offence, and action will be taken," he added.
Article Summary: Sia’s brother said the incident happened on Sunday morning and that they did not inform their parents about it. He said his sister initially did not tell them about the incident, but later informed them that it was a hit-and-run case. Gurgaon Police had earlier said that no written complaint had been received from the victim.

Article Title: Rs 3.5 lakh debt, family dispute: Police save family of 4 from suicide bid on Fountain Bridge near Mumbai
Article Text:
During questioning, police learnt that the man worked as a delivery boy and lived with his family at Shanti Park in Mira Road East.





MIRA ROAD: It was around 2am when a 28-year-old man stood on Fountain Bridge with his wife and their two young daughters, aged one and two, contemplating taking the extreme step.A timely alert to the police control room and swift action by two beat marshals helped save the lives of all four.At around 1.58am on Monday, the Mira-Bhayandar, Vasai-Virar police control room alerted Kashigaon police station that a man was allegedly attempting to end his life along with his wife and two children on Fountain Bridge.Versova beat marshal No. 4, police havaldar Kokre and police constable Mohite, immediately rushed to the area and began patrolling the bridge and its surroundings.At around 2.18am, they located the man and safely took him, his wife and their two daughters into custody, averting a possible tragedy.During questioning, police learnt that the man worked as a delivery boy and lived with his family at Shanti Park in Mira Road East.A few months ago, he had borrowed around Rs 3.5 lakh from his sister after pledging gold. With his financial condition worsening, his sister had been asking him to redeem the gold, sell it and return the remaining amount.Police said the financial strain and the resulting family dispute had left him distressed, prompting him to contemplate taking the extreme step along with his wife and children.The police then counselled the family and advised them to resolve the dispute rather than take any drastic step. His brother and sister were also counselled and asked to resolve the family issue at the earliest."The moment we received the information, the beat marshals were alerted and they immediately rushed to the spot. Their timely intervention helped avert a major tragedy. The family was subsequently counselled," said PSI Harish Patil.What began as a late-night emergency call ended with four lives being saved. A swift police response, followed by counselling, helped bring a distressed family back from the brink of tragedy.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old man stood on Fountain Bridge with his wife and their two young daughters, aged one and two, contemplating taking the extreme step. A timely alert to the police control room and swift action by two beat marshals helped save the lives of all four.
