Article Title: Canada deports Lawrence Bishnoi gang operative Karamveer Deo, held at Delhi airport
Article Text:
Deo was taken into custody by Punjab Police upon his arrival at Delhi airport.





NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on Lawrence Bishnoi ’s international syndicate, Canada has deported Karamveer Deo, a senior operative of the gang. Sources said Deo was one of Bishnoi’s top confidants and was directly privy to the syndicate’s operational moves.Deo was taken into custody by Punjab Police upon his arrival at Delhi airport. The Punjab Police had previously issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him, and he was detained immediately after his flight from Canada landed.Investigations reveal that Karamveer played a critical role in facilitating the escape of Lawrence Bishnoi’s brother, Anmol Bishnoi, from India.Once abroad, Anmol stayed at Karamveer’s residence in the United States, which gained public attention after viral videos showed Anmol partying and dancing with Punjabi singers at the location.Beyond providing safe houses, Karamveer functioned as a primary logistical operator for the gang, offering shelter and legal assistance to Bishnoi syndicate members entering the US.However, as the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intensified its crackdown on the gang’s foreign network, Karamveer fled the US and shifted his base to Canada.Karamveer Deo’s role had also come to light in the firing incident outside Punjabi singer AP Dhillon’s residence in Canada.His eventual deportation marks a significant breakthrough for Indian law enforcement in dismantling the Bishnoi gang’s overseas support system.
Article Summary: Deo was taken into custody by Punjab Police upon his arrival at Delhi airport. The Punjab Police had previously issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him. His eventual deportation marks a significant breakthrough for Indian law enforcement in dismantling the Bishnoi gang’s overseas support system.

Article Title: Gurgaon biker hit-and-run: Cops arrest accused car driver Kalyan Bainsla
Article Text:
Gurgaon Police also issued a stern warning that any attempt to take the law into one's own hands would not be tolerated.





GURGAON: Gurgaon Police on Tuesday arrested accused car driver Kalyan Bainsla after adding an attempt-to-murder charge in the case involving a car allegedly hitting a woman biker on Golf Course Road.Bainsla was arrested in Rajgarh, Rajasthan, Gurgaon CP Sibash Kabiraj said.Police will soon bring the accused to Gurugram.Bainsla, a gym owner who describes himself as an international kabaddi player, said he was travelling with his sister and two cousins when the incident occurred.The case was registered at Sector 56 police station after a video of the incident went viral on social media on Monday, following which police took suo motu cognisance and launched an investigation.During the probe, investigators analysed CCTV footage from the area and, based on their findings, added Section 109 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with attempt to murder, to the FIR, Gurgaon Police said.The provision carries a punishment of up to 10 years, according to the police.Gurgaon Police also issued a stern warning that any attempt to take the law into one's own hands would not be tolerated."Lawlessness will not be tolerated at any cost," the police said, adding that it remained committed to taking strict action against those involved in such offences.“This incident has been unfolding since yesterday. He hit someone, left them on the road to die and drove away, yet he is still roaming around freely. He is giving soundbites to news reporters and presenting his side of the story, ” Sia said.Sia said, “There were only boys in the car, as far as I could see. There were no women. I was heading to a biker’s cafe in Gurgaon. I don’t have a fixed group that I always ride with; sometimes I ride with my brother. Since others own the same bike model as mine, people in the biker community know each other and recognise each other’s bikes. That’s how they recognised me. One of them was someone I knew, with whom I had gone on a couple of group rides. His camera was on, and he recorded everything.”
Article Summary: Kalyan Bainsla was arrested in Rajgarh, Rajasthan, Gurgaon CP Sibash Kabiraj said. Police will soon bring the accused to Gurugram. A video of the incident went viral on social media on Monday.

Article Title: Clicked wedding invite, lost Rs2.75 lakh: Pune retired auditor falls prey to APK fraud
Article Text:
Elderly Pune resident lost over two lakh rupees to online fraudsters. (AI image)





PUNE: Cybercrooks allegedly siphoned off Rs2.75 lakh from a retired auditor (75) of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) by sending him an online wedding invitation card between Aug 31 and Sept 1.The elderly man lodged a complaint with the Kothrud police on Sunday. The retired auditor stated in his FIR that he was alone at home when he received a message on his messaging application from a number similar to his nephew’s cellphone number.He opened the message and saw an online wedding invitation card.An officer from Kothrud police said, “The retired auditor opened the wedding card and later went to sleep. Around midnight between Aug 31 and Sept 1, he started receiving messages from his bank stating Rs20,000, Rs40,000, Rs60,000 and other amounts had been withdrawn from his account. He had neither visited the bank nor an ATM, and realised that the money was being withdrawn from his bank account.”The next morning, he visited the bank and blocked his account. By then, the fraudsters had withdrawn Rs2.75 lakh from it.When he approached Pune cyberpolice, “A police officer checked his phone and found an .apk file downloaded on his cellphone. Inquiry revealed he had downloaded the .apk file by clicking on the wedding invitation card.It was a remote-access software link, and the complainant ended up sharing his banking credentials with the fraudsters after downloading it,” said an officer from the cyberpolice.On June 13 this year, a shopkeeper (53) from Tadiwala Road lodged a complaint with Bund Garden police, saying online fraudsters had siphoned off Rs5.3 lakh from his bank account by sending him an online wedding invitation.On May 21, cybercrooks sent .apk files to two different people and siphoned off money from their bank accounts. The Khadak and Faraskhana police registered two separate complaints against the online fraudsters. The two victims were cheated of a total of Rs8.5 lakh.An APK (Android Package Kit) file is the standard file format used by the Android operating system to distribute and install cellphone apps and games. Online fraudsters misuse .apk files to compromise their targets’ devices.Such files can give fraudsters remote access to a device, allowing them to monitor the cellphone or laptop. Once they obtain banking details, they siphon off money from the victims’ bank accounts.Pune cyber police have appealed to people not to download any file ending with .apk received through a message or a link. People can scan their cellphones and other devices for .apk files. If they find any such file on their devices, they should delete it without delay.
Article Summary: The elderly man lodged a complaint with the Kothrud police on Sunday. The retired auditor stated in his FIR that he was alone at home when he received a message on his messaging application from a number similar to his nephew’s cellphone number. He opened the message and saw an online wedding invitation card.

Article Title: Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mid-interview and tells everyone he cannot take him on ...
Article Text:
Donald Trump's position

A debate already roiling Silicon Valley

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s response

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles took an unexpected turn when US President Donald Trump phoned in mid-conversation, using the moment to publicly dismiss growing concerns about AI posing an existential risk. According to a report by Business Insider, at the All-In Summit the interview of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was interrupted by a phone call from Trump. The interruption began with a bit of stage comedy. As Nvidia CEO scrambled to get Trump patched through on speakerphone, the moment was framed as the president now addressing the entire planet — with a joke about the irony of Huang being able to design the world's most advanced computer chips, yet needing help simply getting a phone connected to a speaker. "See, the great thing about life is that Jensen can develop the most complex computer chip in the world that nobody can copy for 10 years, but he can't figure it out to put me on speaker," said Trump.Speaking via speakerphone, Trump also dismissed the fears of artificial intelligence as alarmist, declaring, “The robots will not be taking over.” He further added that while caution is necessary, the US should not halt AI advancement.Trump described AI doomerism as a “hoax,” reiterating his stance later on Truth Social: “Breaking another Hoax That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World.” His remarks came amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation from Anthropic, where he warned that AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”The interruption landed in the middle of an already heated industry conversation about AI safety. The debate intensified after Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic researcher, announced his resignation from the lab last week, writing on social media that people building the technology believe it could pose a threat to humanity's survival within the decade.During his talk, Huang struck a more measured tone than Trump's, praising Coxon for speaking out about AI safety while also pushing back on the broader idea that AI represents an existential threat, calling that particular framing unscientific. He said AI safety is paramount, while maintaining that the U.S. can continue moving quickly on AI development without sacrificing safety, arguing the country is capable of leading in AI while still doing so responsibly.Huang drew a clear distinction between Coxon's decision to speak up and the broader predictions being made about AI's future. He said he considers whistleblowing about problems inside a company to be legitimate, but views scientific-sounding predictions about the future as considerably less credible, since he argued they aren't actually grounded in science. He added that he doesn't personally know what Coxon witnessed while at Anthropic, and suggested that frontier AI labs more broadly are in the midst of a difficult transition from primarily research-driven organizations into engineering-focused ones.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during an interview. Trump dismisses AI doomerism as a "hoax," reiterating his stance later on Truth Social. His remarks come amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.

Article Title: Five Held In Rohini E-Rickshaw Driver Murder Case
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Five people, including two women, have been arrested in connection with the murder of an e-rickshaw driver in Sector 28, Rohini. A knife allegedly used in the crime, along with the vehicles involved and blood-stained clothes, has also been recovered. The arrested have been identified as Anuj (19), Himanshu (21), Sachin (22), Nandini Tiwari (19) and Kunti (18).The incident took place on the night of Sept 12 following a minor collision between a motorcycle and a scooty.Police sources said Abhishek intervened in an argument that followed the collision. During the altercation, Himanshu allegedly got into a physical fight with Abhishek, who slapped him and caught hold of his neck. Anuj caught Abhishek from behind, while Sachin alias Santosh took out a knife and stabbed him. Abhishek was rushed to a hospital but later succumbed to his injuries. Nandini and Kunti were present with the group at the time of the incident. The three male accused are residents of Shahbad, while the two women are from Jahangirpuri, police added.
Article Summary: Five people, including two women, have been arrested in connection with the murder of an e-rickshaw driver in Sector 28, Rohini. The incident took place on the night of Sept 12 following a minor collision between a motorcycle and a scooty. A knife allegedly used in the crime, along with the vehicles involved and blood-stained clothes, has also been recovered.

Article Title: Yellow Line services impacted by signal issue, restored after 4 hrs
Article Text: New Delhi: The service on a small stretch between Rajiv Chowk and Patel Chowk metro stations on Yellow Line was impacted for over four hours by a signalling issue Monday, causing inconvenience to commuters. As the Metro ran at a restricted speed, commuters claimed that there was a cascading effect on other sections of the line. DMRC ) on X at 10.20 am said there was a delay in train services on Yellow Line between Rajiv Chowk and Patel Chowk metro stations due to a signalling issue. DMRC at 2.42 pm said normal services resumed on the line. Sanjay Singh, a commuter who boarded the metro from Hauz Khas to Central Secretariat, said the train was moving slower than usual.Several commuters took to social media to complain about the delay. A commuter said his 20-minute ride turned into an hour-long journey. Another commuter, Rashmi, said, “My half-day salary has already been deducted. Now who’s gonna pay for that?”In March, train services on the new 9.9-km Deepali Chowk-Majlis Park stretch on Magenta Line were impacted after 1,000 metres of signalling cables were stolen before the start of service. Police arrested one of the suspects at the spot.
Article Summary: DMRC said there was a delay in train services on Yellow Line between Rajiv Chowk and Patel Chowk metro stations. Commuters took to social media to complain about the delay. DMRC at 2.42 pm said normal services resumed on the line.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar attack: No whisper of casteist remark, claims accused
Article Text: New Delhi: “There was not even a whisper of a casteist remark,” self-styled Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed before a court Monday, alleging his arrest under SC/ST Act was politically motivated and the complainant had attacked him during the July Jantar Mantar incident.Appearing before additional sessions judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler for bail, Bhardwaj’s counsel, Umesh Chandra Sharma, argued that Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was absent from the June 23 FIR and was invoked later. “Police issued me a notice on June 27 to appear for questioning, and I appeared on June 29. After that, I was allowed to go. Then, after some political developments, I was arrested on Sept 4. After my arrest, a new FIR (under Pocso Act) was registered,” Sharma claimed.When the judge asked whether the provisions against Bhardwaj were added later, police said the initial complaint had no mention of a casteist slur and it was added when the complainant’s statement was recorded again. Sharma also alleged police were ignoring a video purportedly showing the complainant attacking Bhardwaj.The complainant’s counsel, Swati Khanna, opposed bail, saying Bhardwaj had admitted injuring the girl’s father and threatened her several times.“He has also failed to fully disclose his criminal antecedents and can influence the investigation by tampering with the evidence,” she said, adding that an FIR “isn’t an encyclopaedia” and SC/ST Act could be invoked later.The FIR was initially registered in relation to allegations of hurt and was subsequently expanded to include provisions of SC/ST Act on the basis of a supplementary statement recorded during the investigation. The case had attracted attention after a video surfaced in which Bhardwaj was alleged to have spoken about the Jantar Mantar incident, allegedly claiming to have injured the complainant’s father. The FIR, numbered 0062/2026, now alleges simple hurt and casteist slurs.The court reserved its order for Tuesday. Bhardwaj, arrested by the crime branch on Sept 4 after being detained in Bulandshahr, is in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Self-styled Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj claims his arrest under SC/ST Act was politically motivated. His counsel, Umesh Chandra Sharma, argued that Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was absent from the June 23 FIR. Sharma also alleged police were ignoring a video purportedly showing the complainant attacking him.

Article Title: DCW Takes Suo Motu Cognizance of Sexual Harassment Allegations Raised by JNU Students Against a Professor
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Delhi Commission for Women (DCW) has sought an action-taken report from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) over allegations of sexual harassment reportedly raised by some female students against a professor.The commission took suo motu cognisance of a video circulating on social media in which the students alleged that they had submitted a complaint against the professor to the JNU vice-chancellor in May 2026, but no appropriate action was taken.The students alleged that the university administration attempted to protect the professor, instead of acting on their complaint.DCW said it was not treating the allegations as established facts and had sought a report from the university to ascertain the status of the matter.In a notice issued to the vice-chancellor, the commission sought details of the action taken on the complaint and whether it had been referred to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act. If the complaint was referred to the ICC, the commission said it wanted details of the action taken by the committee and the present status of the inquiry.The commission has also sought the action-taken report along with relevant details.In case no action has been taken, JNU has been asked to state the reasons for the delay.The university has been directed to submit the report within three days.DCW chairperson Lata Gupta said the complaints of sexual harassment raised by the students must be dealt with fairly, promptly and sensitively.She said the commission’s objective was to ensure that every complaint was examined and that complainants were not denied access to justice because of administrative inaction or delay.The commission said it would examine JNU’s report and take further necessary action based on the facts and findings available on record.
Article Summary: Delhi Commission for Women (DCW) has sought an action-taken report from Jawaharlal Nehru University. The commission took suo motu cognisance of a video circulating on social media. The students alleged that they had submitted a complaint against the professor to the JNU vice-chancellor in May 2026.

Article Title: Maharashtra BJP MLA Parag Shah dresses as beggar to experience ‘reality of life’ on Jain guru’s advice
Article Text:
BJP MLA Parag Shah





MUMBAI: Maharashtra BJP MLA Parag Shah, one of the state’s richest legislators, recently gave up his security detail, cars and expensive belongings to dress as a beggar and spend a day seeking alms on the streets of Ghatkopar, an experience he said gave him a glimpse of the “reality of life”.A video of the Ghatkopar (East) MLA dressed as a beggar went viral on social media, leaving many viewers surprised before the reason behind his unusual exercise emerged.Shah, a businessman, undertook the exercise on the advice of his Jain spiritual guru Namramuni during the ongoing special month, considered significant in Jain religious tradition.Following his guru’s suggestion, Shah stayed away from his security arrangements, vehicles and expensive belongings. He also underwent makeup to avoid being recognised and spent several hours on the streets in the guise of a beggar."All the respect and honour, the people who line up to meet you -- the same people, when I go to them, become taller than me. So, that is the reality of life," Shah maintained while recounting his experience.The BJP politician noted the exercise also showed him the helpful nature of the people in Mumbai."Someone gave me Rs 20 saying, 'Go baba, eat food'. There was a samosa seller there.I went to him and took a samosa, and he gave it without any charge. I saw one thing, Mumbai city is such that people here are always ready to help one another," Shah recounted."And that is my own experience'¦ when I told the samosa seller that I did not have money, he still gave me the samosa with a smile 'the man was very small, a poor hawker ' but without making a face even once, he gave me the samosa," he said.Shah, who is active in the real estate sector, not only sought alms but also consumed the food he received and sat by the roadside like a beggar. He later narrated the experience to his guru and other people.After removing his makeup, Shah revisited some of the places he had visited while dressed as a beggar and spoke to the same people again. The exercise allowed him to reflect on their reactions without them knowing his identity at the time.Shah is known for his considerable wealth. In his affidavit filed for the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, he had declared assets worth more than Rs 3,383 crore, making him the state’s richest candidate at the time.The realtor-turned-politician has also served as a corporator of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.(With Agency Inputs)
Article Summary: M Maharashtra BJP MLA Parag Shah, one of the state’s richest legislators, recently gave up his security detail, cars and expensive belongings to dress as a beggar. Shah, a businessman, undertook the exercise on the advice of his Jain spiritual guru Namramuni.

Article Title: Banned scavenging killed them; their families now wait years for Rs 30L relief
Article Text:
UP native Ratanlal Jaiswar’s son Chandan died in a septic tank in 2024. He has been living in Taloja, painting vehicles for a living and waiting for the compensation

Sewer deaths in Maharashtra





Arjun Chauhan (37) knows he should not be doing it. The contract worker from Panvel knows septic tanks and sewers are to be cleaned by machines, not people. He knows protective gear is mandatory. But when the call comes, he climbs in, with no safety cover.Chauhan has been doing this for 15-20 years, taking work from contractors, buildings and housing societies. A contractor pays him Rs 700-1,000 a day; others Rs 1,500-2,000. "There are lakhs like me who do this. After all, I have to put food on the table for my family," he said.His story is the reality behind the ban on manual scavenging: people continue to enter septic tanks, and when they die, their families spend years waiting for the statutory Rs 30 lakh compensation.For Ratanlal Jaiswar (54), that wait began in Dec 2024, when his son Chandan (22) died cleaning a septic tank at a chawl in Uran. Chandan, along with Vikas Kisan Tak (33) who too died, had entered the tank to rescue another worker who had collapsed inside.An FIR lodged was against the contractor, a suction-truck owner and one of the homeowners-all of whom had employed them to clean the tank without safety equipment.Nearly two years later, Ratanlal paints vehicles for a living and is awaiting the money.He wants to leave Taloja and return to UP, where his family is, and use the money to get his four children married. "I don't know how long I have to wait. Work dries up during monsoon, and when I don't find work, I sit here and sleep," he said.Tak's family is struggling too. They say the police initially refused to lodge an FIR, while the suction-truck owner offered to take care of the deceased's child's education. However, the family maintained that it wasn't enough as Tak was the sole breadwinner. His widow Archana (22), his mother and his sister Muskan now do domestic work to pay the rent for their room in Asudgaon, Panvel. Tak, who used to work as a driver-cleaner on the suction truck as well as do septic tank cleaning work, was paid Rs 17,000 a month, mostly in cash."I want my five-year-old son to complete his education. He is now my only hope to get out of this situation," Archana said.The same cycle has played out in other parts of Mumbai.In Powai, Akshay Mandal (23) andFulchand Kumar Saw (29) died in Nov 2025 while cleaning a sewage plant. "He was running the house. He used to send money so we could buy food and celebrate festivals," his father Jaynarayan, who travels to Mumbai from Jharkhand each year for work, says. Mandal's family got Rs 10 lakh from the contractor on humanitarian grounds but is awaiting the statutory compensation.Manual cleaning of manholes, septic tanks, and sewers is banned in India. But National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data shows 332 sanitation workers died in 18 states and UTs during hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks between Jan 1, 2021 and June 30, 2026. Maharashtra had the highest number of deaths at 58. Data tabled in the House in July 2025 by the state showed zero deaths in Mumbai between 2021 and 2024; a figure disputed by activists. Centre too has maintained that a survey found no manual scavengers in India."They want to hide the reality of caste-based discrimination. They don't accept the situation of Dalits who do scavenging," said Milind Ranade of Maharashtra Municipal Kamgar Union. He said the deaths reflect an indifference that has allowed the practice to persist. "The attitude remains: They are born to serve. Mar rahe hain, marne do."In the case of Jaiswar and Tak, the state said that since a private contractor engaged them, the compensation must be recovered from the employer. Bombay high court, however, held in Aug that the state must pay even when workers are privately engaged, and can recover it later from employers. It struck down Item 11 of 2019 and 2025 GRs, which forced private societies or contractors to pay instead of the state.Meanwhile, some families are awaiting enhanced compensation after Supreme Court, in 2023, raised it to Rs 30 lakh and directed govts to provide rehabilitation, including employment for next of kin and education for children.Nearly seven years after three workers died cleaning a tank in Govandi in 2019, each widow received Rs 10 lakh, but the balance has been pending. "It should've been released automatically. We have been trying to reach the authority, but there is no response. The approach remains casual," said advocate Abha Singh, who is pursuing the cases pro bono.Bezwada Wilson, national convenor of Safai Karmachari Andolan, says the delays show larger failure: "The govt has yet to acknowledge the extent to which manual scavenging continues, let alone identify those still trapped in it."But for those still doing the work, the distinction between what is legal and what happens on the ground is less important than the next day's wages. So when the next call comes, workers like Chauhan continue to climb into sewers.
Article Summary: Manual cleaning of manholes, septic tanks, and sewers is banned in India. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data shows 332 sanitation workers died in 18 states and UTs during hazardous cleaning. Maharashtra had the highest number of deaths at 58. Data tabled in the House in July 2025 by the state showed zero deaths in Mumbai.

Article Title: Chembur cat killer gets bail day after arrest, activists upset
Article Text:
Shiva was arrested by the RCF police on Friday night based on CCTV footage and accounts of two eyewitnesses.





MUMBAI: Twenty-four hours after Chembur's suspected serial cat killer, a 40-year-old homeless man identified as Shiva, was arrested, he was released on bail on Saturday, leaving animal lovers and activists alarmed.Shiva was arrested by the RCF police on Friday night based on CCTV footage and accounts of two eyewitnesses.He was charged under section 325 of BNS and other sections of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. Police suspect him of killing more than 20 cats and kittens found dead in Panjrapol and surrounding areas since August.Local cat feeder Rubeena Pathan told TOI, "We were initially relieved when the accused cat killer was nabbed by the RCF police on Friday night. However, by Saturday afternoon, he was bailed out after being produced in court. This means that he is once again a free man and can harm more animals."Pathan said Shiva had allegedly confessed to killing several cats because they disturbed him and had also shown police where he had buried the felines. "However, now that he has been released, we don't know if he can be traced again," she said. Animal rights group PETA India expressed disappointment over the release and said it would approach senior Mumbai police officers seeking his re-arrest.The group had earlier announced a Rs 50,000 reward for information leading to the identification of the suspected serial cat killer.PETA India has also urged DCP Sameer Shaikh to add relevant provisions of the NDPS Act for alleged possession of marijuana, reportedly recovered from Shiva when he was arrested.Senior psychiatrist Dr Anjali Chhabria said suspected drug use and homelessness warranted psychological evaluation. She said marijuana can cause psychosis in some people and may contribute to violent behaviour.Psychiatrist Dr Shefali Batra said the discovery of around 20 dead and mutilated cats over a period indicated possible premeditation and ritualistic behaviour. She said the perpetrator may be expressing underlying rage, powerlessness or a need for control through vulnerable animals. Since August, at least 20 cats and kittens have been found dead.
Article Summary: Shiva was arrested by the RCF police on Friday night based on CCTV footage and accounts of two eyewitnesses. He was charged under section 325 of BNS and other sections of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. Police suspect him of killing more than 20 cats and kittens found dead in Panjrapol and surrounding areas.

Article Title: Confident all 21 NDA-governed states will have UCC by 2029: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah addresses the media in Mumbai on Sept 13

Mumbai:





Union home Amit Shah on Sunday expressed confidence that Uniform Civil Code (UCC) will be introduced in all 21 NDA-governed states before 2029.“Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced UCC in several states and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA-governed states, we will introduce UCC before 2029,” he told reporters.Asked whether the 1951 baseline would be used for implementing National Register of Citizens (NRC) in Manipur , Shah said the Union govt is holding discussions with its allies and other political parties over it. “Whatever decision is taken, we will inform you,” he said.He said govt had ended five decades of Maoism and signed more than 14 peace agreements in the the northeast region. “More than 9,000 people have surrendered and today we have taken the northeast on the path of development.”Shah refused to disclose the methods being deployed to identify illegal Bangladeshi migrants and their detection in cities such as Mumbai. “You are asking the home minister to make the tools public and tell you how it will be done. Then how will we catch them? They will also come to know,” he quipped. He reiterated govt’s resolve to identify and deport infiltrators from the country.On national security, Shah said the dilution of Articles 370 and 35A had been achieved without a single drop of blood being shed or a bullet being fired, and asserted that Kashmir was now fully integrated with India.He said surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.Asked whether a white paper would be released on the Rs 25,000-crore Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank scam case, allegedly involving the late Ajit Pawar, deputy CM Sunetra Pawar and their nephew NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar, amid conflicting findings by state and central agencies, Shah said agencies were doing their work. A state police inquiry cleared all those who were accused of wrongdoing by ED. A court subsequently discharged all accused in the money-laundering case.He said govt had strengthened the country’s criminal justice system through Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and claimed that several states had recorded a 30% increase in the conviction rate in a single year.Shah outlined NDA allies’ monthlong nationwide campaign—Seva Sankalp Abhiyan—beginning Sept 17 to mark PM Narendra Modi’s 25 years in top administrative positions. He also listed out people-oriented schemes implemented by the Modi-led govt across the country. He was accompanied by CM Devendra Fadnavis and deputy CM Eknath Shinde.
Article Summary: Union home Amit Shah expressed confidence that Uniform Civil Code (UCC) will be introduced in all 21 NDA-governed states before 2029. Shah refused to disclose methods being deployed to identify illegal Bangladeshi migrants and their detection in cities such as Mumbai.

Article Title: Decolonisation doesn’t mean wiping out of history, it’s a must: Amit Shah
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah at an exhibition organised by the Asiatic Society of Mumbai

Mumbai:





Decolonisation does not mean the erasure of history, Union home minister Amit Shah said on Sunday, asserting the need to free history from colonial-era fetters and rebutting allegations made against the PM Modi-led govt that it was trying to wipe out the past.Criticising the British Empire for instrumentalising Indology “in order to maintain and consolidate its power and to destroy the confidence” of the Indian people, Shah said the original purpose of Indology was neither enlightenment nor welfare. Distinguishing between German and British Indologists by specifically referring to the British colonisers, Shah said they used Indology to understand Indian systems so that they could rule over Indians for a long time. “Today, we are freeing knowledge from that grip to present the truth to the world,” he said.Shah’s comments came at a function at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and could be seen as an unapologetic response to charges of “takeover of institutions” hurled at BJP and other ideological affiliates of the Sangh Parivar, especially so as the remarks came on an occasion at which he was invited to see the Society’s rare collections by its newly-installed committee said to be ideologically inclined towards BJP, with former party MP Vinay Sahasrabuddhe as president and two other former MPs as key office-bearers.“The process of decolonisation is a must. It means presenting history to people again with a complete, authentic, and Indian perspective,” Shah said, setting out the aims, as he sees them, of the Society’s new establishment.Shah made a distinction between an external power that “studies a civilisation” and “one that seeks to define a civilisation”. A study, if sincere, could even bring about a change in the thinking of such a power, he said. But India’s colonisers, he argued, had carried out their study for their own aims. “Indian knowledge wasn’t being written in India’s voice but in the colonial power’s language,” Shah said.On how the entire approach to Indology—which “emerged as a study of archaeology, history, epigraphy, literature, linguistics, grammar, Darshan Shastra, Dharma Shastra, among other subjects”—was abused, he said, “When a people’s self-confidence is shattered, they do not offer resistance against this state of slavery for a long time. India’s treasure of knowledge had deliberately been defined to ensure such an outcome. ”India’s knowledge tradition, which has at its core the well-being of the universe, had survived despite repeated attempts to destroy it, Shah said. Citing Nalanda’s example, he said, “One can burn the library of Nalanda, but the knowledge that resides in people’s minds as Smruti (memory) and Shruti (oral traditions of texts), no one can destroy.”“Today, the country has become independent. More than 80 years have passed. Now, the govt has also changed, so has the Asiatic Society’s committee. Now this treasure trove of knowledge, for long lying unused, will be used for welfare of the universe, country, and world. Such a path will certainly be paved,” he said, urging the Society to “preserve Indian knowledge systems, history, traditions, languages, manuscripts and archives” and take these across the country and the world.“The British tied up the idea of knowledge with power. Our task is to detach knowledge and power, so that power itself flows from knowledge and is structured around it,” Shah said.At a time when BJP is being accused of historical revisionism through an ideological lens, Shah said, “True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology. If you bind it in any way, you change the very meaning of knowledge. Knowledge should be free and uninhibited, and its declaration should also be free and uninhibited.”He urged that the collected works of P V Kane, author of the monumental five-volume study of The History of Dharmashastra, be brought out by the Society. He outlined a three-point strategy for the Society: to seek and invite scholars wanting to take a deep dive into its collections; to digitise its entire collection and share it with societies and libraries across India; and to build a unified platform for all such institutions under its aegis.Shah was accompanied by CM Devendra Fadnavis, deputy CM Eknath Shinde and state education minister Chandrakant Patil.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah spoke at an exhibition organised by the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. Shah said the original purpose of Indology was neither enlightenment nor welfare. “Today, we are freeing knowledge from that grip to present the truth to the world,” he said.
